call_input.prompt:
Use case: ads-marketing
Asset type: one finished portrait poster, 2:3 aspect ratio, full-bleed flat artwork.

Create a single compelling poster for the Korean title given below. The specific visual idea is the act of blooming: a tight flower bud becomes a partly opened cup and then a fully opened flower, all visibly part of one coherent plant and one growth language. Make this unfolding action determine the large silhouette, the empty intervals, and the placement of the title. This is one continuous artwork, never a diagram, three panels, a contact sheet, or a mockup.

Scene and image: a deep midnight blue-green ground. One slender, bent botanical stem rises from the lower left into a broad diagonal sweep toward the upper right. It carries exactly three substantial floral forms: a narrow closed bud at the left, a cupped half-open flower toward the middle, and a large fully opening flower toward the upper right. Give all three the same recognizable elongated petal and sepal structure so that closure changing into openness is obvious without any explanatory labels. The petals become progressively wider apart; the final flower is a loose radial fan with visible dark gaps between individual petals. Keep the sepal cups and branching joints intelligible. The largest open bloom reaches close to the upper and right edges, with one deliberate petal crop; the bud and half-open flower remain complete. Do not make a bouquet of unrelated species. Use only a few necessary pointed leaves at the actual branching joints.

Medium and surface: precise flat screenprinted botanical silhouettes, with warm bone-white petal faces and restrained muted jade-blue petal undersides, against the solid blue-green night ground. The image is graphic, not a photograph or a glossy 3D object. Use clean intentional edges, a very faint genuine print grain, and consistent two-tone shading which describes the curling and opening petals. No glow, stars, moon, decorative circles, random flecks, frames, or floating effects.

Typography and spatial relationship: print the supplied title as one readable occurrence, divided only at its two word spaces into three word groups. Arrange the three groups in their ordinary left-to-right reading order across the open lower-middle diagonal clearing: the first group low on the left beneath the closed bud, the second group slightly higher in the interval beneath the half-open cup, the last group higher again beneath the open fan. This gradual rising baseline follows the independently visible opening action. Use the same strong, generous, plain Korean Gothic letterform for every syllable, warm bone-white, with crisp complete Hangul strokes and normal internal syllable spacing. Each word is a compact cohesive group; the two word intervals are visibly broader. The title must be large enough to read in a small poster preview. Flowers remain images and never replace, grow from, or alter the Korean syllables. Preserve clear dark breathing room around each word and avoid accidental contact with stems or petals.

First view: see the widening arc from bud to open blossom. Then read the title in its rising three-word rhythm. Leave the bottom quiet enough to make the single sweeping stem legible; do not fill it with ornaments. All parts share a single restrained print language.

Text (verbatim, sole permitted copy, exactly once): 밤에 피는 정원
The title has three Korean words with one visible word separation between each. No quotation marks, other text, captions, stage labels, Latin letters, numbers, signatures, logos, watermark, or extra marks.

요청한 화면 비율을 유지하면서 현재 도구와 모델이 지원하는 가능한 최대 해상도로 출력. Preserve the portrait 2:3 ratio. Return one flat finished poster only.

residuals: Middle cup and final curling lily fan show a broad stylized shape change; identical species reading is uncertain.
Title uses three broadly separated rising word groups, so reading follows a diagonal path.
Upper/right petal cropping is intentional and leaves the complete final flower outline unseen.
Maximum supported generation resolution is not confirmed.
